fields.statement: At bf5b09b2 I built rhiza into a scratch dir and ran it by hand in a scratch repo with a bare origin, RHIZA_* unset. I opened a change set with change new in the main checkout, which left two untracked .rhiza/log dirs. I copied them into a git worktree on branch cs, added a feature commit, pushed it, and squash-merged it into origin/main from a second clone. ship close-out --forget exited 0 with main_updated true and update-main done. Main HEAD equalled origin/main, git status was clean, and the log entries were tracked. Second case: I appended bytes to one untracked log file that origin/main also held. close-out exited 1 with update-main failed, and the detail named that file. The file stayed untracked with its tampered bytes (cmp equal). The matching copies beside it were dropped. Third case: an untracked .rhiza/log/stray.json that origin lacks stayed put, and close-out still updated main. go test ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/ship-close-out -count=1 passes.

At bf5b09b2, with a scratch build in a scratch repo: ship close-out --forget failed at update-main (exit 1, main_updated false) because a differing untracked log file blocked the pull, and .git/rhiza/ship/<cs>.json was still there. I removed the blocking file and re-ran the same ship close-out --forget. It exited 0 with main_updated true, main HEAD equal to origin/main, and the state file gone. In the first case, a successful --forget close-out also removed its state file.
